title: Proposal: Support image formats in `<video>`

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body: > [!NOTE] > 👉🏼 [**Explainer here**](https://github.com/webplatformco/explainers/blob/main/images-in-video/README.md) by me & @frivoal > The following is a summary. cc @whatwg/media ### What problem are you trying to solve? This originally came up due to Bloomberg needing to address this in their mail client, but the problem is much broader: image galleries, nearly all user generated content, social media, etc. There are many instances where website authors need control over playback of animated images. In some cases this is to improve user experience (e.g. in a gif gallery), in other cases to guard against untrusted input, and in others to follow WCAG practices and e.g. disable `autoplay` on `(prefers-reduced-motion)`, show controls etc. Goals: * Provide website authors playback control over animated images, allowing them (at a minimum) to control playback and looping * Authors should not need to create their own playback UI to provide this functionality to their users * Authors should have full styling control over playback UI, either by customizing UA-generated UI, or recreating it, and ideally both. * Provide a way for authors to embed visual media without having to detect format and branch Non-goals: * Controlling animation of CSS images * Retrofitting all images on a page to not animate, without making HTML changes These are valuable (and may target them separately), but out of scope for this proposal, which targets the most pressing issue for user-generated content. ### What solutions exist today? The web platform currently provides no way to do this, so all current solutions are computationally expensive and have serious limitations. They mainly revolve around server-side processing (to extract frames or convert to video) or extracting frames by painting on canvas which does not work cross-origin and thus makes it a poor solution for user-generated content. Since this is often desired for accessibility, it cannot require a heavyweight special setup that is out of reach for smaller publishers, or only work some of the time. The explainer goes into a lot more [specifics](https://github.com/webplatformco/explainers/blob/main/images-in-video/README.md#user-research) on this. ### How would you solve it? Allowing images on `
